title: LoRa frequencies by country
summary: Which LoRa band, power limit and duty cycle apply in 211 countries and territories, with the matching LoRaWAN plan and Meshtastic region. Also covers ham use, antenna gain and matching a radio's hardware band to your region.

steps.text: Find your country in the country index and note its plan, then read that plan's row in the band-plan table for frequency, power and duty cycle.
steps.warn: Fit the antenna before you power up and transmit. Antenna gain counts against the EIRP or ERP limit, so a bigger antenna can mean turning the radio down.

steps.text: Set the radio to match: the Meshtastic region (it will not transmit until one is set), the MeshCore regional preset, or the LoRaWAN plan.
Before you buy, build or salvage, check that the band on the module's label or part number (433, 868 or 915 MHz) matches your plan.
Licensed ham? Read the amateur section: more power, but no encryption and you must send your call sign.

notes:
LoRa uses licence-free bands whose limits change by country. Find your country in the index, then read its plan in the band-plan table.

**Power words.** Conducted power is measured at the antenna socket. ERP is measured against a half-wave dipole, EIRP against an isotropic antenna: EIRP = ERP + 2.15 dB (TTN EIRP). mW = 10^(dBm ÷ 10): 10 dBm = 10 mW, 14 = 25 mW, 20 = 100 mW, 27 = 500 mW, 30 = 1 W, 36 = 4 W (TTN dB).

**Duty cycle** is the share of each hour you may transmit: 0.1 % = 3.6 s, 1 % = 36 s, 10 % = 6 min (ERC Rec 70-03). **Dwell time** is the longest stay on one channel. **LBT**: listen before talk.

### US, Canada and Australia: power rules

- **US** (FCC 15.247). Covers only hopping and digital modulation. Hops under 250 kHz wide: 50+ channels, 1 W conducted, ≤0.4 s per channel in 20 s. Wider hops: 25+ channels, 0.25 W if under 50. Digital modulation: 500 kHz+ wide, 1 W, ≤8 dBm per 3 kHz. Antenna over 6 dBi: cut power 1 dB per extra dB.
- **Canada** (ISED RSS-247). Same hopping rules. 50+ hop channels, or digital modulation: 1 W conducted, 4 W EIRP. Under 50: 0.25 W conducted, 1 W EIRP.
- **Australia** (ACMA LIPD). 915–928 MHz: 1 W EIRP, gain included, for hopping on 20+ frequencies, or digital modulation at ≤25 mW EIRP per 3 kHz. Anything else: 3 mW EIRP.

## Country index

From the country table in RP002-1.0.5 (2025): 248 ISO countries and territories, 206 with a band (LoRa Alliance RP002). Five more come from TTN's list alone. Meshtastic regions are from its country page (Meshtastic regions); disagreements are from TTN's (TTN). Rules change: RP002 says it is not an authoritative source of government rules, and crowd-sourced lists like TTN's and Meshtastic's can lag.

- A range after a plan is the country's own band where it differs from the plan's. "(no plan)": band listed, no LoRaWAN plan named.
- RP002 footnotes: [1] AU915 also fits; [2] only 915–928 usable; [3] AS923 groups also fit; [4] AS923-1 favoured by big Australian operators; [5] US915 also fits; [6] CN779 deprecated; [7] rules expected to change; [8] rules recently changed.

## Licensed amateur radio

Hams can run LoRa on amateur bands with more power, under amateur rules.

- **Bands.** US: 33 cm, 902–928 MHz (the Americas only), and 70 cm, 420–450 MHz; elsewhere it is often 430–440 MHz (FCC Part 97). Canada: 430–450 and 902–928 MHz on a Basic qualification (ISED RBR-4).
- **Power.** US: Meshtastic cites the 10 W PEP limit for spread spectrum; use the least power that works (Meshtastic FAQ, FCC Part 97). Canada, Basic: 190 W carrier (ISED RBR-4).
- **No encryption.** The US bans messages encoded to hide their meaning (FCC Part 97). Canada allows only codes that are not secret, and only with other hams (Radiocommunication Regulations).
- **Call sign.** US: at the end of each contact and every 10 minutes (FCC Part 97). Canada: at the start and end, and every 30 minutes (ISED RBR-4).
- **Where.** US 33 cm use is restricted in parts of Texas, New Mexico, Colorado and Wyoming (FCC Part 97).
- **Meshtastic.** Set your long name to your call sign, then turn on "Licensed amateur radio" (Android) or "Licensed Operator" (Apple). Ham regions such as ITU2_70CM appear only in licensed mode, and licensed and unlicensed nodes cannot talk. Many countries ban encryption (Meshtastic FAQ, Meshtastic LoRa).

## Practical rules

- **Match the board to your band.** The SX1278 covers only 137–525 MHz, so it cannot do 868 or 915 MHz (Semtech SX1278). Wide-range chips (SX1262: 150–960 MHz) still ship on per-band boards, like Semtech's 915 MHz North America and 866 MHz India boards (Semtech SX1262) or RAK3172 -8 (EU868, RU864, IN865), -9 (US915, AU915, KR920, AS923) and -43 (EU433) (Meshtastic RAK).
- **Match the antenna** to the frequency: 50 Ω, often SMA. RP-SMA does not interchange with SMA (Meshtastic antennas).
- **Never transmit without an antenna.** Reflected power can damage the radio (Meshtastic antennas). In Meshtastic, turn off Transmit Enabled while swapping antennas (Meshtastic LoRa).
- **Gain counts.** EIRP = transmitter dBm + antenna dBi − cable loss dB; for ERP use dBd = dBi − 2.15 (TTN EIRP). US or Canada: 30 dBm + 6 dBi = 36 dBm EIRP (4 W), Canada's cap (ISED RSS-247); with a 9 dBi antenna, drop to 27 dBm (FCC 15.247). Europe, 869.4–869.65 MHz: cap 27 dBm ERP (ERC Rec 70-03); with a 5 dBi (2.85 dBd) antenna and 1 dB cable loss, set the radio to about 25 dBm (TTN EIRP).
- **Set the region.** Meshtastic will not transmit until it is set (Meshtastic LoRa). In MeshCore pick your region's preset (US/Canada: 910.525 MHz) and set repeaters to a legal frequency (MeshCore FAQ).
- **Keep duty-cycle limits on**; Meshtastic's override can break EU rules. Nodes need the same region and preset to hear each other (Meshtastic LoRa).

## When no help is coming

Nobody may be checking, but the bands are shared. Licence-free radios must not cause harmful interference and must accept it (FCC 15.5). In the US, 902–928 MHz also carries government radiolocation, location monitoring and hams (FCC 15.247, FCC Part 97); 433 MHz is inside the 70 cm ham band (FCC Part 97), where hams may pass emergency messages (Radiocommunication Regulations). Staying in band and within power keeps you off their signals and on your mesh's settings, so people can hear you (Meshtastic LoRa).
